heroHeadline: Exiled Opposition Leaders Unite as US Pushes OAS Toward Action Ahead of Oct. 2 Meeting
heroSubtitle: Secretary of State Marco Rubio pressed allies September 24 to 'stop business as usual' with Managua ahead of the OAS foreign ministers' October 2 session, as exiled Nicaraguan opposition figures — including former Sandinista commander Dora María Téllez — set aside old civil-war divisions to jointly call for international intervention. The same day, US ambassador nominee Natasha Franceschi told her Senate confirmation hearing she would keep up 'diplomatic pressure' on Ortega-Murillo, while Nicaragua's co-foreign minister met Russia's Sergei Lavrov at the UN General Assembly to reaffirm ties. Separately, exiled journalist Luis Galeano was freed on bail September 25 after 11 days in US immigration detention, and the government authorized limited religious events for the weekend while a researcher said 407 parishes remain restricted.
